messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — running the async streaming tests locally and hitting a weird failure only on my machine. CI (linux, GH actions) green.
sahil: what error you seeing?
maria: Streaming request fails with `TypeError: async_generator object is not iterable` coming from our wrapper in client/stream.py: we iterate with `for chunk in resp.aiter_text()` which used to be fine.
jamie: that sounds like an httpx/httpcore mismatch. Which httpx version do you have? and python version?
maria: python 3.10.11, httpx 0.24.1, httpcore 0.16.3, poetry-managed venv. On CI we pin httpx 0.24.0 though (from lockfile).
lina: there was a breaking change around aiter_text -> aiter_bytes behavior between httpx minor versions. Also some distros ship an older `spoofed` typing-extensions.
sahil: can you paste pyproject and poetry.lock snippet? also any difference between `poetry run` vs `pip install -e .`?
maria: pyproject toolchain part:
```
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "^3.10"
httpx = "^0.24.0"
typing-extensions = "^4.5"
```
But my poetry.lock ended up with httpx 0.24.1 due to transitive resolver picking httpcore 0.17.0
jamie: yup, that explains it. CI's lockfile is strict so GH actions installs exact versions. Locally, if you `poetry install` without --lock or with different resolver state, you can diverge.
maria: i always run `poetry install` though. I suspect my global pip + editable install path flagged something when running tests via `pytest -q`.
lina: a common local flake: outdated pip/setuptools/wheel produce a different build wheel for httpcore extras. Try `python -m pip install -U pip setuptools wheel` then `poetry lock --no-update && poetry install --no-root` to reproduce CI packages.
sahil: or `poetry export -f requirements.txt --without-hashes | python -m pip install -r /dev/stdin` to mirror CI exactly.
maria: ok trying that now... hold
maria: ok that fixed streaming iteration error. But another thing: type checking fails in CI for `types-requests` mismatch: my pyright complains about `typing_extensions.Literal` import location.
jamie: we saw that in a recent PR — typing-extensions bounds need tightening. Can we update pyproject to pin typing-extensions to <5.1 for py3.10? or better, change code to `from typing import Literal` with fallback to typing_extensions.
lina: small snippet for fallback pattern:
```
try:
    from typing import Literal
except Exception:
    from typing_extensions import Literal
```
sahil: also consider adding a devex checklist to README: recommended local setup commands (upgrade pip, export lock, run tests via `poetry run pytest`) so new folks don't hit this.
maria: good call. I'll add a short section and a one-liner `poetry run python -m pip install -U pip setuptools wheel`.
jamie: for the SDK dependency change — can you open a tiny PR to pin typing-extensions and add the fallback? i'll review.
maria: created draft PR #452 and added a note: "pin typing-extensions to avoid py3.10/3.11 divergence; add runtime fallback for Literal". @jamie please review when you have a sec.
devex-bot: Reminder: check the contributor guide for dependency changes. link: https://go.redwood.dev/devex/deps-guide
sahil: thanks — once PR merged we should run a fresh lock + `poetry export` and update the CI cache key.
jamie: i'll take CI changes. lina can you add the README snippet?
lina: on it, will push a small commit to the draft PR.
maria: thanks team, reopening local env after doing the pip upgrade fixed the tests. leaving the thread for follow-ups on the PR. :thumbsup:
